title: HOOK//30 ASCENSION (recognition, transformation, payoff)
frameRule: frame = round(swung(beat) * beatSeconds * 44100); beatSeconds = 0.625 at 96 BPM; the file loops, so frame 1323000 is frame 0

movements.development: B1 note for note in voice, bass, mallets and clock, with bowed bars holding the harmony and a kick and damped spring marking the bass riff. Dm | Bb | Gm C | Dm A7

deceptive arrival on B-flat. A low second voice sings the hook, rising each bar; the lead follows two beats later, twice at its original pitch, so the same notes are reharmonised by a bass that climbs a semitone per bar (tines mark the line three octaves up). The lead hangs on the seventh of A7; silence; one breath; the pickup returns with a B natural. Bb | G7/B | C7 | A7/C#

the hook in D major with the second voice a sixth below; answered a fourth higher (the highest note of the piece); the same reach darkened to G minor while bars and tines trade the stretto, speeding from eighths to triplets to sixteenths; the inverted cadence over a dominant pedal back to D minor. D | G | Gm C7/E | Dm/A A7b9
